1	# Reference Code — Patterns to Port
2	
3	These are real working patterns from sibling projects. When architecture says "port from references.md",
4	describe the shape to port — not the implementation detail.
5	
6	## financing-plugin — Claude Code Plugin Structure
7	
8	The gold standard for a well-structured Claude Code plugin.
9	Location: `~/Projects/financing-plugin-extracted/`
10	
11	### Plugin Layout Pattern
12	```
13	plugin-name/
14	├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json   # Plugin metadata + version
15	├── agents/                      # Specialised agents as flat .md files
16	├── hooks/                       # SessionStart hook (context injection)
17	├── references/                  # Convention references (single source of truth)
18	├── skills/                      # Skills — each a SKILL.md
19	│   ├── SKILL_MAP.md             # Master index of all skills
20	│   ├── feature-pipeline/SKILL.md   # Orchestrator skill
21	│   ├── feature-requirement/SKILL.md
22	│   └── dev-build/SKILL.md       # Dev tools
23	└── docs/                        # Spec-doc specs (Epic, Architecture)
24	```
25	
26	Key rule: **references are the source of truth** — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills.
27	Skills read from `references/*.md`, never inline the same constraint twice.
28	
29	### SessionStart Hook Pattern
30	The hook fires on every session start and injects live context into the agent.
31	No heavy I/O — just read files and compute a snapshot. Fast and deterministic.
32	
33	### Skill File Pattern (SKILL.md)
34	```markdown
35	# Skill Name
36	
37	## When to use
38	[Trigger conditions]
39	
40	## What I do
41	[Steps the agent takes]
42	
43	## Tools available
44	[Bash, Read, Write, etc.]
45	
46	## Examples
47	[Sample invocations]
48	```
49	
50	## OpenClaw Workspace Files — Context Injection Pattern
51	
52	The workspace files already loaded by OpenClaw every session:
53	- `AGENTS.md` — session instructions (auto-loaded)
54	- `USER.md` — who Sam is (auto-loaded)
55	- `MEMORY.md` — curated long-term memory (auto-loaded in main session)
56	- `TOOLS.md` — stack + environment (auto-loaded)
57	
58	Port pattern: new skills should reference these files rather than duplicating their content.
59	`SOUL.md` defines agent identity — skills can refer to it for tone/style.
60	
61	## spec-doc Bootstrap Adapter — Async 202 + Polling Pattern
62	
63	Already shipping in spec-doc. Port this pattern for any long-running skill:
64	1. POST trigger → return 202 + job_id immediately
65	2. Background thread runs the work
66	3. GET /status/{job_id} polls until `done: true`
67	4. In-process dict keyed by project/job id — no Redis needed
68	
69	Location: `~/Projects/2026/spec-doc/api/modules/ai/routes/text.py` (bootstrap)
70	and `~/Projects/2026/spec-doc/api/modules/ai/routes/task_gen.py` (generate-task)
71	
72	## Trendfy — Docker + Deploy Pattern
73	
74	gunicorn config for Flask with background threads:
75	```
76	gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:3101 --workers 1 --threads 4 --timeout 900 --worker-class gthread
77	```
78	`--workers 1` required when using in-process state dicts (no cross-worker sharing).
79	`gthread` allows daemon threads to coexist with gunicorn.
80	
81	## humanize-me — Flask Thin Layer Pattern
82	
83	Flask as a ~150 line AI service boundary:
84	- All routes: validate → call AI adapter → return streaming or JSON
85	- No business logic in routes
86	- Supabase accessed only through Flask, never from frontend directly

1	# 🏗️ Solution Architecture: Modular Restructure
2	
3	**Purpose**: Long-lived system design document.
4	
5	**References**: Addresses [Analysis](./analysis.md). See [Epic](./epic.md) for scope.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Architecture Overview
10	
11	`api/modules/` currently holds 10 flat peer packages. The flat shape was appropriate at 3 modules because the groupings were obvious; at 10, the conceptual clusters — AI generation, execution infrastructure, storage, and pipeline quality — exist only in the developer's head. The filesystem offers no signal. Every new SaaS module added without a restructure deepens that silence until `modules/` becomes a 17–20 entry index that requires prior knowledge to navigate.
12	
13	The restructure externalizes the existing mental model into four named packages: `ai/` (all generation routes, prompts, and services), `runtime/` (chain adapter and workflow engine), `data/` (projects, context, templates), and `quality/` (pipeline self-improvement, already cohesive). Future SaaS capabilities — auth, billing, usage, observability — land as independent peer packages at the `modules/` root, not sub-domains of the four core packages. The structural test enforces this boundary so the sprawl cannot re-emerge silently.
14	
15	The change is purely mechanical: file moves and import-path rewrites. No function body is touched, no route URL changes, no Blueprint names change, no DTOs drift. `make test` passes before the first file moves (scaffold) and must pass again after the last import fix (import rewrite). The diff is large in line count and zero in semantic content.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Design Principles
20	
21	| Principle | Application |
22	|-----------|-------------|
23	| ELA #1 — Adapter Boundary | `modules/runtime/chain/adapter.py` remains the sole AI import point; its internal path changes but its role does not |
24	| ELA #2 — Blueprint Module Structure | `routes.py`, `service.py`, `prompts.py` ownership per module is preserved; files move, not their responsibility split |
25	| ELA #5 — Not-Yet-Built | `runtime/` is described as the concrete `chain/` + `workflows/` pair it houses today, not as a generic runner framework |
26	| ELA #6 — Workflow Domain Layer | `runtime/workflows/` continues to own `WorkflowRuntime` and `AbstractStep`; AI-specific workflow definitions live in `ai/workflows/` |
27	
28	---
29	
30	## System Boundaries
31	
32	### What This System Includes
33	
34	- Four top-level packages (`ai/`, `runtime/`, `data/`, `quality/`) replacing 10 flat modules
35	- `__init__.py` scaffolding for each new subdirectory before any source files move
36	- File relocation for 16 source files per the confirmed mapping in the Epic
37	- Import-path rewrites for ~50 `from modules.X import Y` references across routes, services, `create_app.py`, and tests
38	- An updated `ENABLED_MODULES` block in `create_app.py` pointing to new dotted import paths
39	- A `packages_areInExpectedHierarchy` assertion in `tests/test_structural.py` that pins the 4-package boundary and documents the `saas_optional` allowlist decision
40	
41	### What This System Does NOT Include
42	
43	| Excluded | Reason |
44	|----------|--------|
45	| Logic changes of any kind | Constraint is absolute; zero semantic change in this refactor |
46	| API URL changes | Blueprint URL prefixes live in Blueprint declarations, not file paths |
47	| Blueprint name changes | `spec_gen_bp`, `task_gen_bp`, etc. are the registered app names; import path is separate |
48	| `openapi.yaml` changes | The contract is independent of package layout |
49	| Test assertion changes | Test logic moves with its module; only file location and import paths change |
50	| SaaS module code (auth, billing, usage, observability) | This epic creates their slots; each SaaS capability is its own epic |
51	| Per-package `CLAUDE.md` files | `api/CLAUDE.md` remains the single source of truth |
52	| `dtos/` relocation | Generated artifact at api root; stays where `datamodel-codegen` writes it |
53	| Renaming `quality/` to `pipeline/` | Separate concern, separate PR |
54	| Splitting `chain/` into sub-packages | Exactly one consumer (`ai/`) exists today; ELA #5 prohibits speculative splits |
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Component Design
59	
60	### `ai/` Package
61	
62	**Purpose**: Consolidates all AI generation: the six text endpoints, spec generation, task generation, and implementation guide prompts. These three flat modules shared the chain adapter through the same workflow runtime and had no meaningful boundary between them — grouping them makes their coupling an asset, not noise.
63	
64	**Key Parts**:
65	- `ai/routes/text.py` — was `modules/ai/routes.py`; consumed by Angular frontend via HTTP
66	- `ai/routes/spec_gen.py` — was `modules/spec_gen/routes.py`; consumer: Angular spec generation view
67	- `ai/routes/task_gen.py` — was `modules/task_gen/routes.py`; consumer: Angular task view with 202 polling
68	- `ai/services/spec_gen.py` and `ai/services/task_gen.py` — pure business logic; no Flask imports
69	- `ai/prompts/` — all prompt-construction functions; consumers are the service files above
70	- `ai/workflows/spec_gen/generate_spec.py` — AI-specific Workflow definition; consumed by `ai/services/spec_gen.py` through `runtime/workflows/`
71	
72	**Patterns**: ELA #2 (routes own no logic; services own no Flask); ELA #6 (Workflow definitions owned by the domain that uses them, not the runtime that runs them)
73	
74	---
75	
76	### `runtime/` Package
77	
78	**Purpose**: Generic execution infrastructure that the `ai/` package depends on but does not own. `chain/` provides the adapter boundary; `workflows/` provides the execution engine. Neither has consumers outside `ai/` today — they live in `runtime/` because they are infrastructure, not because they are shared.
79	
80	**Key Parts**:
81	- `runtime/chain/adapter.py` — sole AI import point; provider selected by `CHAIN_PROVIDER` env var; consumer: every service in `ai/`
82	- `runtime/chain/providers/` — `cli.py` and `anthropic_sdk.py` behind the adapter interface
83	- `runtime/workflows/runtime.py` — `WorkflowRuntime` execution driver; consumer: `ai/services/spec_gen.py`
84	- `runtime/workflows/repository.py` — `WorkflowRepository` FS adapter; consumer: `WorkflowRuntime`
85	- `runtime/workflows/steps/` — `AbstractStep`, `AICall`, `Compute`; consumer: `ai/workflows/spec_gen/`
86	
87	**Patterns**: ELA #1 (adapter boundary enforced); ELA #6 (runtime drives, domain defines)
88	
89	---
90	
91	### `data/` Package
92	
93	**Purpose**: All filesystem-backed storage and content retrieval. `projects/`, `context/`, and `templates/` were already peers conceptually — grouping them names the boundary explicitly.
94	
95	**Key Parts**:
96	- `data/projects/service.py` — `get_project()`, `update_file()`, `list_projects()`; consumers: `ai/` routes and `quality/` pipeline
97	- `data/context/service.py` — `read_context()`, `write_context()`; consumers: `ai/` prompt builders
98	- `data/templates/` — deterministic generators (spec-index, timeline, README); consumer: Angular template view via HTTP
99	
100	**Patterns**: ELA #2 (service files only; no Flask in business logic)
101	
102	---
103	
104	### `quality/` Package
105	
106	**Purpose**: Pipeline self-improvement linter. Already cohesive; moved in place. Sits at `modules/quality/` before and after the restructure.
107	
108	**Key Parts**: Unchanged — whatever `quality/` contains today is preserved exactly.
109	
110	**Patterns**: Treated as a peer top-level package, not a sub-domain of the four core packages.
111	
112	---
113	
114	### Structural Shape Test
115	
116	**Purpose**: Prevents silent re-sprawl. The `packages_areInExpectedHierarchy` test asserts that every directory under `modules/` is either in the four-package set, in the `saas_optional` allowlist, or fails CI. Any engineer adding a fifth top-level package must explicitly acknowledge it in this test — the PR diff makes the decision visible.
117	
118	**Key Parts**: One test function in `tests/test_structural.py`; one inline comment recording the `saas_optional` allowlist decision and its rationale. Consumer: CI pipeline.
119	
120	---
121	
122	## Design Decisions
123	
124	| Decision | Rationale | Trade-offs |
125	|----------|-----------|------------|
126	| Nest packages under `modules/{ai,runtime,data,quality}/` | The cluster boundary is conceptual, not cosmetic; a real namespace should reflect it | One extra import segment in every `from modules.X` reference; ~50 mechanical edits |
127	| SaaS modules as peer top-level packages, not sub-domains | Auth, billing, usage, observability are independent capabilities with their own routes, services, and DTOs; forcing them under `ai/` or `data/` would be a false grouping | `modules/` root grows by one entry per SaaS module; the structural test manages this with an explicit allowlist |
128	| `quality/` stays at top level, unchanged | It's already cohesive and has no sibling that belongs beside it inside one of the three core packages | Asymmetry with `ai/runtime/data/` hierarchy — `quality/` is flat while peers are nested; acceptable given it's already correct |
129	| `chain/` stays whole inside `runtime/` | Exactly one consumer (`ai/`) exists today; ELA #5 prohibits splitting for a single consumer | If a second non-AI consumer of the chain adapter emerges, `runtime/chain/` may need to become a public cross-package API |
130	| Exhaustive `saas_optional` allowlist vs naming convention | Decision deferred to Task 1 inspection — must be resolved before Task 5 codes the test | Exhaustive list is safe but requires a PR edit for each new SaaS module; naming convention is open-ended but harder to audit |
131	| Scaffold directories before moving files | `make test` can pass between Task 2 and Task 3; broken imports only exist between Task 3 and Task 4 | One extra task boundary; reduces the blast radius of a mid-move interruption |
132	
133	---
134	
135	## Execution Flow
136	
137	```
138	Task 1 (read-only)
139	  Confirm module inventory + resolve 3 open questions
140	  → Outputs: confirmed file-by-file mapping, saas_optional decision
141	
142	Task 2 (additive only)
143	  Scaffold directory trees + __init__.py stubs
144	  → make test must pass
145	
146	Task 3 (moves only)
147	  Relocate 16 source files per confirmed mapping
148	  → Imports intentionally broken; make test expected to fail
149	
150	Task 4 (import rewrites)
151	  Rewrite ~50 from-modules imports; update ENABLED_MODULES in create_app.py
152	  → make test must pass; no assertion changes
153	
154	Task 5 (pin structure)
155	  Add packages_areInExpectedHierarchy to tests/test_structural.py
156	  → make test must pass; saas_optional decision from Task 1 encoded inline
157	```
158	
159	---
160	
161	## Open Questions
162	
163	- **Does `implementation_guide/routes.py` exist?** If it does, it needs a Blueprint entry in `ENABLED_MODULES`; if it doesn't, it's prompt-only and needs no route registration. Inspection in Task 1 resolves this before any files move.
164	
165	- **Does `quality/` register a Blueprint in `create_app.py`?** If yes, `ENABLED_MODULES` must include the (unchanged) `modules.quality.routes` entry. If no, it's a service-only module and requires no update. Task 1 resolves this.
166	
167	- **Exhaustive `saas_optional` allowlist or naming-convention check?** An exhaustive `{"auth", "billing", "usage", "observability"}` set is auditable and fails loudly for any unexpected name; a convention check (`name in known_saas_names or name.startswith("saas_")`) is more open-ended. The correct answer depends on whether the four named SaaS modules are the complete set or an open-ended list. Task 1 must record the decision; Task 5 must encode it with the rationale inline.
168	
169	---
170	
171	## Related Documents

173	- [Analysis](./analysis.md) – Problems driving design
174	- [Epic](./epic.md) – Scope and tasks
175	- [Timeline](./timeline.md) – Status tracking
176	- [Spec Index](./spec-index.md) – Document overview

1	# Engineering Principles — Sam's Projects
2	
3	Non-negotiable across all projects. When a brain dump contradicts a principle, the analysis step must flag it.
4	
5	## P1 — Adapter Boundary
6	All external service calls (AI, DB, storage, HTTP) go through a single adapter module.
7	No feature code imports a provider directly. The adapter is the only file that knows which provider is active.
8	- spec-doc: `modules/chain/adapter.py`
9	- OpenClaw plugins: wrap external calls in a dedicated skill or tool wrapper
10	
11	## P2 — Thin HTTP Layer
12	Route handlers contain no business logic. Handlers: validate input → call service → return response.
13	- Flask: `routes.py` handles HTTP only; `service.py` holds pure Python logic
14	- OpenClaw: skill files describe tool invocations; no inline logic
15	
16	## P3 — Async 202 + Polling for Long Operations
17	Any operation > 30s returns 202 immediately with a job identifier.
18	A background thread does the work. A status endpoint lets the client poll until `done: true`.
19	No HTTP connection held open. No Redis — in-process state keyed by job/project id.
20	
21	## P4 — No Speculative Abstractions
22	Build for the one concrete case that exists now. No generic runners for one consumer.
23	No base classes for one subclass. No registries for one item.
24	Three similar lines of code is better than a premature abstraction.
25	
26	## P5 — OpenAPI-First (spec-doc)
27	`openapi.yaml` is the contract. DTOs are generated from it. Never hand-edit generated files.
28	Routes implement the contract — not the other way around.
29	
30	## P6 — OpenClaw Plugin Principles
31	- Skills first: start with `SKILL.md` files (no build step, iterate fast)
32	- Graduate to `openclaw.plugin.json` package only when skills hit real limits
33	- References are the single source of truth — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills
34	- Agents are declarative descriptions, not imperative code
35	- Context files (`MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, `TOOLS.md`) are loaded every session — keep them current
36	- Boot hooks fire on session start — keep them cheap (no blocking I/O)
37	- Channel-aware: skills must adjust output format per channel (Telegram ≠ web UI)
38	
39	## P7 — File Size & Structure
40	- Files under 200 lines (hard target, not a guideline)
41	- Named exports only (no default exports in Angular/TS)
42	- One component per file
43	- Build verification required before each commit (Angular: `ng build --configuration production`)
44	
45	## Code Rules
46	- No direct push to master — always PRs; PRs target master; live is deploy branch
47	- Daemon threads only (`daemon=True`) — never block server shutdown
48	- Empty context strings handled gracefully — callers never crash on missing context
49	- `read_context()` returns `""` for missing files; `PromptBuilder.section()` skips empty content
50

3	---
4	
5	# 🏗️ Text Chains — Architecture
6	
7	**Purpose**: Technical design for chain operations.
8	
9	**References**: See [Epic](./epic.md) for scope. See [Analysis](./analysis.md) for constraints.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Overview
14	
15	Text Chains adds three layers on top of the existing /text infrastructure: a context-block loader, a chain runner with step-handler dispatch, and chain definitions as static JSON. All three are server-side, inside their own module boundaries. The frontend extends the /text page with a second button row and a tabbed output area for multi-file results. No new services beyond the two new modules. No new database tables — existing `superapp_generations` gets two metadata columns (`chain_id`, `step_count`) via Alembic migration.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Design Principles
20	
21	| Principle | Application |
22	|-----------|-------------|
23	| Feature = Bounded Context | Context loader and chain runner are separate modules with structural tests enforcing their boundaries |
24	| Adapter (every feature service) | Context loader is adapter-shaped: `CONTEXT_PROVIDER=mock` returns fixture strings. Chain runner calls Claude exclusively through the existing chain adapter |
25	| Strategy (AI providers) | Chain definitions declare operations by name; `STEP_HANDLERS` dispatch map resolves to the correct adapter call without if/elif |
26	| Observer (cross-feature events) | `chainCompleted` event emitted on every chain run — analytics subscribes without coupling to the runner |
27	| Feature Guard with Null Object | Disabled `text_chains` → locked buttons with "Pro" badge, never hidden. Backend returns 403 with upgrade hint, never 404 |
28	| Registry (feature flags) | `text_chains` in user's `enabled_features`. Blueprint registered in `ENABLED_MODULES`. Per-chain gating shape named but not built |
29	| Anti-Corruption Layer | File markers (`===FILE:===`) parsed server-side into structured `{name, content}` objects — LLM output format doesn't leak to frontend |
30	
31	---
32	
33	## System Boundaries
34	
35	```
36	┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
37	│  /text page (Angular)                                 │
38	│  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────────┐   │
39	│  │ Single-shot keys │  │ Chain-mode keys (new)    │   │
40	│  │ Rewrite, Expand  │  │ Deep Humanize, BrainDump │   │
41	│  │ Compress, Clarify│  │ Rewrite+Review           │   │
42	│  │ Generate         │  │ [locked if !text_chains] │   │
43	│  └────────┬────────┘  └────────────┬─────────────┘   │
44	│           │                        │                  │
45	│  AiService.rewrite()    AiService.chainRun()          │
46	│  AiService.generate()   POST /api/text/chain          │
47	└───────────┼────────────────────────┼──────────────────┘
48	            │                        │
49	            ▼                        ▼
50	┌───────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────────────────┐
51	│  Existing text    │   │  chain.runner (new)           │
52	│  endpoints        │   │  ┌─────────────────────────┐ │
53	│  /api/ai/text/*   │   │  │ STEP_HANDLERS dispatch  │ │
54	│                   │   │  │ rewrite → handle_rewrite │ │
55	│                   │   │  │ generate → handle_generate│ │
56	│                   │   │  │ review  → handle_review  │ │
57	│                   │   │  └────────────┬────────────┘ │
58	│                   │   │               │              │
59	│                   │   │  Loads ChainDefinition JSON   │
60	│                   │   │  Loads context via loader     │
61	│                   │   │  Calls chain.adapter per step │
62	│                   │   │  Emits chainCompleted event   │
63	└───────────────────┘   └──────────────┬───────────────┘
64	                                       │
65	                        ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
66	                        │              │              │
67	                        ▼              ▼              ▼
68	            ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
69	            │ chain.adapter│  │ context/     │  │ chain/       │
70	            │ (existing)   │  │ loader.py    │  │ definitions/ │
71	            │              │  │ manifest.json│  │ *.json       │
72	            │ → Claude API │  │ prompts/     │  └──────────────┘
73	            └──────────────┘  │ rubrics/     │
74	                              └──────────────┘
75	```
76	
77	---
78	
79	## Component Design
80	
81	### Context Block Loader (`server/modules/context/loader.py`)
82	
83	**Purpose**: Adapter-shaped module that resolves context-block names to markdown content.
84	
85	**Interface**:
86	```python
87	def load_block(name: str) -> str
88	def load_blocks(names: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]
89	```
90	
91	**Manifest** (`server/context/manifest.json`):
92	```json
93	{
94	  "humanize-pass-1": "prompts/humanize-pass-1.md",
95	  "humanize-pass-2": "prompts/humanize-pass-2.md",
96	  "humanize-pass-3": "prompts/humanize-pass-3.md",
97	  "braindump-lint": "prompts/braindump-lint.md",
98	  "braindump-to-docs": "prompts/braindump-to-docs.md",
99	  "builder": "prompts/builder.md",
100	  "principles": "prompts/principles.md",
101	  "references": "prompts/references.md",
102	  "quality-rubric": "rubrics/quality.md"
103	}
104	```
105	
106	- Paths resolved relative to `server/context/`
107	- Missing block → `KeyError` with block name in message (fail loud, not silent empty string)
108	- Missing file on disk → `FileNotFoundError` with full path (catch mismatches between manifest and filesystem)
109	- **Mock mode**: `CONTEXT_PROVIDER=mock` returns deterministic fixture strings keyed by block name. Same interface, no file I/O. Controlled via env flag in `conftest.py`.
110	
111	**Structural invariant**: only `context/loader.py` reads from `server/context/`. Enforced by grep-based structural test:
112	```python
113	def test_contextFiles_onlyReadByLoader():
114	    # grep server/ for open()/read_text() referencing server/context/ outside loader.py
115	    # fail: "Only context/loader.py may read from server/context/. Use loader.load_block(name)."
116	```
117	
118	### Chain Runner (`server/modules/chain/runner.py`)
119	
120	**Purpose**: Given a chain definition + user input, execute steps sequentially through the chain adapter.
121	
122	**Step Handler Dispatch**:
123	```python
124	STEP_HANDLERS: dict[str, Callable] = {
125	    "rewrite": handle_rewrite,   # adapter.rewrite(text, mode, context)
126	    "generate": handle_generate, # adapter.generate(prompt, context)
127	    "review": handle_review,     # adapter.generate(review_prompt, context) → JSON
128	}
129	```
130	
131	Adding a new operation = one function + one dict entry. The runner loop iterates `definition.steps`, looks up the handler by `step.op`, calls it with the current text + resolved context blocks, and passes the output as input to the next step. No if/elif. No switch-case.
132	
133	**Multi-file parsing**: when `definition.outputMode == "multi-file"`, the runner scans the final step's output for `===FILE: {name}===` markers and splits into `[{name, content}]`. This is an anti-corruption layer: the LLM output format (marker-delimited) is parsed into a structured response before reaching the frontend.
134	
135	**Observer**: on completion, emit `chainCompleted` signal:
136	```python
137	emit("chainCompleted", {
138	    "chainId": definition.id,
139	    "stepCount": len(definition.steps),
140	    "inputLength": len(user_input),
141	    "outputLength": len(final_output),
142	    "totalTokens": sum(step_tokens)
143	})
144	```
145	Mirrors the existing `outputCompleted` pattern from the UX revamp. Analytics, future cost dashboard, and usage-limit enforcement subscribe to this event without importing from the chain module.
146	
147	**Error handling**: if any step fails, return `{ error: str, partialOutput: str, failedStep: int }`. Don't swallow the error. Don't retry (retry/backoff machinery is deferred infrastructure — trigger: when a real failure teaches us a retry budget).
148	
149	**Structural invariant**: only `chain/runner.py` reads from `chain/definitions/`. Grep-based test:
150	```python
151	def test_chainDefinitions_onlyReadByRunner():
152	    # grep server/ for open()/json.load() referencing chain/definitions/ outside runner.py
153	    # fail: "Only chain/runner.py may read from chain/definitions/. Use runner.load_definition(chainId)."
154	```
155	
156	**Deferred infrastructure** (not built, triggers named):
157	- `RunnerAdapter` interface → extract when a second execution strategy appears (parallel, streaming, retry)
158	- Per-chain feature gating resolver → extract when pricing tiers diverge per chain
159	- `chain_call` + `chain_signal` tables → extract when cost tracking becomes a reporting requirement, not just a logging concern
160	
161	### Chain Definitions (`server/modules/chain/definitions/*.json`)
162	
163	Chain definitions live **inside** the chain module boundary. Each definition is a JSON file:
164	
165	```json
166	{
167	  "id": "deep-humanize",
168	  "name": "Deep Humanize",
169	  "steps": [
170	    { "op": "rewrite", "mode": "humanize", "context": ["humanize-pass-1"] },
171	    { "op": "rewrite", "mode": "humanize", "context": ["humanize-pass-2"] },
172	    { "op": "rewrite", "mode": "humanize", "context": ["humanize-pass-3"] }
173	  ],
174	  "outputMode": "single"
175	}
176	```
177	
178	```json
179	{
180	  "id": "braindump-to-docs",
181	  "name": "Brain Dump → Docs",
182	  "steps": [
183	    { "op": "review", "context": ["braindump-lint"], "outputKey": "lint" },
184	    { "op": "generate", "context": ["builder", "principles", "references", "braindump-to-docs"] },
185	    { "op": "review", "context": ["quality-rubric"], "outputKey": "score" }
186	  ],
187	  "outputMode": "multi-file"
188	}
189	```
190	
191	```json
192	{
193	  "id": "rewrite-review",
194	  "name": "Rewrite + Review",
195	  "steps": [
196	    { "op": "rewrite", "mode": "user-selected", "context": [] },
197	    { "op": "review", "context": ["quality-rubric"] },
198	    { "op": "rewrite", "mode": "fix", "context": [] }
199	  ],
200	  "outputMode": "single"
201	}
202	```
203	
204	**Schema fields**: `id` (string, unique, used as `chainId` in API), `name` (human-readable label for UI), `steps` (ordered array), `outputMode` (`"single"` or `"multi-file"`). Each step: `op` (must exist in `STEP_HANDLERS`), `mode` (optional, operation-specific), `context` (array of block names from manifest), `outputKey` (optional, names the output for downstream reference).
205	
206	### API Endpoint (`POST /api/text/chain`)
207	
208	**Request**: `{ chainId: string, input: string }`
209	
210	**Response** (single-file): `{ generationId: string, result: string }`
211	
212	**Response** (multi-file): `{ generationId: string, files: [{name: string, content: string}] }`
213	
214	**Error** (feature-gated): `403 { error: "text_chains not enabled", upgrade: true }`
215	
216	**Error** (chain not found): `404 { error: "Chain definition not found: {chainId}" }`
217	
218	**Error** (step failure): `500 { error: string, partialOutput: string, failedStep: number }`
219	
220	- Blueprint registered in `ENABLED_MODULES` — same registration pattern as existing feature modules
221	- Feature-gated via middleware: checks `user.enabled_features` for `text_chains`
222	- Persists to `superapp_generations` with `chain_id` + `step_count` columns
223	- Alembic migration adds the two columns (nullable, backfill not needed — existing rows have `NULL`)
224	
225	### Frontend: Chain Mode UI
226	
227	**AiService extension** (`src/app/services/ai.service.ts`):
228	```typescript
229	export interface ChainResponse {
230	  generationId: string;
231	  result?: string;
232	  files?: Array<{ name: string; content: string }>;
233	}
234	
235	chainRun(chainId: string, input: string): Observable<ChainResponse> {
236	  return this.http.post<ChainResponse>(`${this.baseUrl}/chain`, { chainId, input });
237	}
238	```
239	
240	**OperationBarComponent extension** (`src/app/components/operation-bar/operation-bar.component.ts`):
241	- Second `.operations` row with chain buttons
242	- Each button emits a `ChainOperationEvent` with `chainId`
243	- Buttons have `data-test` selectors: `data-test="chain-deep-humanize"`, `data-test="chain-braindump"`, `data-test="chain-rewrite-review"`
244	- **Null-object guard**: when `textChainsEnabled` input is `false`, buttons render with `opacity: 0.5`, "Pro" badge, click shows upgrade toast instead of executing
245	- **Step progress**: during chain execution, loading indicator shows "Step N of M..." (derived from chain definition step count + progress callback or polling)
246	
247	**Tabbed output area** (new, within existing output region):
248	- Renders when response has `files` array
249	- Tab per file: label = `file.name`, content = `file.content`
250	- Copy-per-tab button with `data-test="chain-copy-tab"`
251	- Active tab tracked via signal, persists during session
252	- Single-file chains render in existing output area with no tabs
253	
254	### Feature Guard — Null Object Fallback
255	
256	| Layer | Behavior when `text_chains` disabled |
257	|-------|--------------------------------------|
258	| Frontend buttons | Visible, locked (`opacity: 0.5`), "Pro" badge, tap → upgrade toast |
259	| Backend endpoint | `403 { error: "text_chains not enabled", upgrade: true }` |
260	| Chain definitions | Still loaded (no conditional logic in runner init) |
261	| Context blocks | Still available (loader is independent of feature flags) |
262	
263	Never hide. Never 404. The user knows the feature exists and what it costs to unlock.
264	
265	---
266	
267	## Execution Flow
268	
269	```
270	[Phase 1 — Foundation]  (parallel)
271	   Task 1: Context Block Loader ──┐

5	# Task 4: Angular Polling Client — Implementation Guide
6	
7	## 1. Context
8	
9	Task 4 wires the Angular application to the new async bootstrap contract introduced by Task 2 (T2). Before T2, `POST /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project` held the connection open for the full 10–25 minute chain and returned 200 with all files — an HTTP connection that infrastructure outside the app's control terminates silently. T2 replaces that with a 202+`job_id` response in milliseconds and a separate `GET /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project/status/{job_id}` polling endpoint. T4's job is purely on the Angular side: two new methods in `ai.service.ts` (`startBootstrapProject`, `getBootstrapStatus`) and a `setTimeout`-based polling loop in `new-project.component.ts` that waits for `status.done`, re-throws on `status.error`, and navigates with `status.files` after the first terminal read — without issuing a second GET. This is a hard cutover; the old synchronous `bootstrapProject` method is removed entirely.
10	
11	**Trade-offs considered:**
12	- **RxJS `interval` + `takeUntil`** — rejected because it obscures the "resolve on first terminal read" invariant and requires a Subject to clean up; `setTimeout` recursion expresses the loop's exit condition more directly.
13	- **SSE / WebSocket for progress streaming** — rejected for this task; that is the province of the `braindump-streaming-task-gen` epic; the `partial` field arrives via that path once it lands.
14	- **`setTimeout` loop + `firstValueFrom`** — preferred; minimal RxJS footprint, terminal condition is explicit in one place, and the 3 s fixed interval is trivially extensible to jitter without restructuring.
